submodules.contenido:
**Kabbalah** is the mystical tradition of Judaism, which tries to understand the **structure of reality**, of the **human soul** and, therefore, of God.

Its purpose is to **find the lost balance again** by understanding the structure of the human soul.

According to tradition, it's a wisdom passed down orally from **Abraham** and **Moses**; but it takes shape in the Middle Ages, in the south of France and in Spain.

Its foundational book is the **Zohar** ("Splendor"), a vast mystical commentary on the **Torah** written in Aramaic, which speaks of God, the origin of the universe, the soul and redemption.

Academic research holds that it was written in thirteenth-century Spain by the kabbalist **Moses de León**.

Later, in the sixteenth century, Rabbi **Isaac Luria (the ARI)**, in the city of Safed, expanded the knowledge of this tradition.

*The Kabbalah we study is the fruit of centuries of transmission, concealment and reinterpretation.*

The **Ein Sof** wished to experience itself from different points of view; and so it manifested in two forms: the **giver** and the **receiver**.

*Love can't be given if there's no one to receive it.*

That's why it manifested as **Or**, the divine light, the giver, the masculine energy; and as **Kli**, the vessel, the receiver, the feminine energy.

We are our own receiver for the light of our soul, which is an extension of the Ein Sof.

**God is contained in every atom**; *the fact that we can't see it doesn't mean it isn't there.*

Spirituality, according to Kabbalah, needs matter in order to manifest.

*Spirituality is a commitment to reality instead of an escape from it.*

Every construction or intellectual goal of a person is part of their spiritual growth.

*A person's energy is the **interconnection** between all the dimensions that make them up.*

*The material world is the place where the spiritual work is done.*

**Creation** isn't a finished product but an **ongoing process**, and the human being completes it through their acts in the world.

Matter is neither an obstacle nor a sin, but the tool of **rectification**.

The rectification of the world through our actions is called **Tikkun Olam**.

**People's central problem is that they don't understand the purpose of their existence**, so they take refuge in administrative tasks that only manage to dissociate them from reality.

---

*Our Life is full of interferences that we ourselves allow in order to avoid our higher purpose.*

We have to set a limit on those interferences, which are sent by our soul in order to put us back in place so we don't forget ourselves.

*Every day is an opportunity to work on our essence, and it's never coming back.*

---

*Everything exists to fulfill a particular function, and that function is what gives that existence its value.*

Part of our purpose is to be aware that everything out there is an extension of us and of our essence.

**Everything and everyone, we're all part of the Ein Sof.**

***Self-improvement** is a form of refinement.*

The level of my refinement is measured by the development it took to reach what I reach, not by what I've already reached.

---

**Happiness** is the consequence of knowing that my Life has meaning; it's the consequence of taking the actions that bring me closer to the balance of the dimensions that make me up.

***Laziness** is failing to give meaning to every minute of our Life.*

If we keep an imbalance going in some dimension, it's because we find some kind of benefit in the suffering of that imbalance.

The rectification of the world is called **Tikkun Olam**: the final repair of the universe.

*Every time we perfect ourselves, we're perfecting the world. We're all part of the same thing.*

---

**Teshuvah** is the act of recognizing where we've failed so that we can accept where we have to change.

*Teshuvah literally means "return": the way back to Love after recognizing the error.*

**Freedom** is the **responsibility** of shaping the direction we want to be led in.

*Real freedom is discovering the meaning of my own Life.*

---

Avoidance isn't only not doing something; it's also doing a great deal without a concrete direction.

*It's wasting time in motion.*

**What matters isn't the movement, it's the direction**, because without it the movement is useless.

*When the enjoyment of sharing is greater than the enjoyment of accumulating, you reach one of the most refined forms of **wisdom**.*

You shouldn't accumulate without the idea of giving: if we want light, we have to give light.

*You shouldn't be a false keeper.*

Whoever hides their knowledge and keeps it to themselves is showing that they don't trust what they know.

**The wise one doesn't want to lose or to win: they want to get closer to the truth.**

---

*If we really want to judge, we can't do it from our own structures and beliefs, but from those of the person we want to judge.*

Whoever receives more does so because they're ready to receive the energy and the responsibility that what they receive demands.

**You can't receive more without being grateful for what you already have; if you're not grateful for what you have, you won't be able to be grateful for more.**

opciones: A) Because the universe needs opposing forces to stay stable.
B) Because the Ein Sof wished to experience itself from different points of view.
C) Because matter was created to contain spiritual energy.
ejercicios.enunciado: According to the text, what is the fundamental reason why Or and Kli appear?

opciones: A) They're developing their spirituality all the same, through action.
B) They're fulfilling their purpose even though they don't know it yet.
C) They may be avoiding themselves through constant motion.
ejercicios.enunciado: If someone devotes their whole Life to productive activities but has no clear direction, the text would say that:

opciones: A) The world is finished and the human being has to adapt to it.
B) Creation continues and the human being takes an active part in it.
C) Rectification belongs to the spiritual plane and nowhere else.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which statement fits best with the idea of Tikkun Olam presented in the text?

opciones: A) Feeling guilty about the mistakes you've made.
B) Avoiding thinking about past mistakes again.
C) Recognizing the error in order to understand what has to change.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which of the following situations best reflects the concept of Teshuvah?

opciones: A) They'd have trouble valuing whatever they receive afterward.
B) They'd be accumulating too much knowledge.
C) They'd become excessively dependent on other people.
ejercicios.enunciado: Following the internal logic of the text, what problem would someone have who wants to receive more without being grateful for what they already have?

opciones: A) Matter is a necessary limitation that in the end has to be left behind.
B) Matter is the means through which spirituality can manifest.
C) Matter and spirituality belong to independent dimensions.
ejercicios.enunciado: What is the relationship between spirituality and matter according to this introduction?

opciones: A) Reaching the highest possible level of well-being.
B) Discovering and carrying out your own function within creation.
C) Getting recognition for your individual abilities.
ejercicios.enunciado: If everything exists to fulfill a function and that function gives its existence value, then personal purpose consists mainly of:

opciones: A) "I'm worth more the more I've accumulated."
B) "My development is measured by what I own."
C) "What matters is who I had to become to achieve what I achieved."
ejercicios.enunciado: Which of the following sentences best expresses the idea of refinement?

opciones: A) Because knowledge loses value when it isn't shared.
B) Because receiving light also implies passing it on.
C) Because wisdom depends on social recognition.
ejercicios.enunciado: Why does hiding knowledge contradict the spiritual logic described in the text?

opciones: A) They're building spirituality through discipline.
B) They're living through a necessary stage before awakening.
C) They run the risk of having disconnected from their essential purpose.
